title: Critical lower bound on average cost
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$ be monotone, nonconstant, and invariant under a transitive action of coordinate permutations. Let $p_*$ be the unique number in $(0,1)$ at which the polynomial giving the probability of output $-1$ under the $p$-biased product distribution equals $1/2$, and put $\\sigma_* = \\sqrt{4p_*(1-p_*)}$. Every finite randomized decision tree computing the real-valued version of $f$ has average query cost under the $p_*$-biased product distribution at least $\\bigl(n/\\sigma_*\\bigr)^{2/3}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$f$ is invariant under a transitive action of coordinate permutations
$T$ is a randomized decision tree computing the real-valued version of $f$
caveat: The excerpt uses the critical probability and its uniqueness through upstream declarations whose defining statements are not included; the description of the associated polynomial follows their names and the supplied definitions.
